# Echoes of Spira: actions and implementations ledger

<!-- Generated by tools/actions-ledger.mjs from docs/target/actions.json. Edit the data, not this file. -->

The central record of everything **done** on the project since it began on 2026-09-15: what was built (implementations, art installs), what was carried out (deploys, reviews, records, infrastructure, account moves, downloads, maintenance, process changes), who did it, which decisions it carried out, and the evidence. Its sibling ledgers are `CHANGELOG.md` (player-facing, one entry per live build) and `DECISIONS.md` (Bailey's decisions, `docs/target/decisions.json`). Dates are Eastern time. The project began as Pyrefly Reprise and is called Echoes of Spira since 2026-10-04; internal names keep "pyrefly".

Rows group sensible units of work, never one row per commit: a feature lane, a fix batch, an art install, one deploy, one review, one clean-up. "Who" names Bailey, the driver session (the main chat that plans and coordinates), a lane (a sub-agent doing one track), a side session or an outside session. Evidence that exists only in the driver's own notes is marked "(not in the repo)".

## How to add a row

1. Append one line to the `actions` array of `docs/target/actions.json` (one entry per line; never edit, reorder or renumber an old row; the next id is the last id plus one, even when the work is older):

   `{"id":"A-0000","date":"YYYY-MM-DD","kind":"deploy","title":"...","what":"...","who":"...","decisions":["D-000"],"game":"both","result":"...","evidence":["commit abc1234"],"reversible":{"value":true,"how":"..."}}`

2. Run `node tools/actions-ledger.mjs` to regenerate this file. `node tools/actions-ledger.mjs --check` exits 1 when the data is malformed or this file is stale; `tests/unit/actions-ledger.test.ts` runs the same checks.
3. `kind` is one of `implementation`, `art`, `deploy`, `review`, `records`, `infrastructure`, `account`, `download`, `maintenance`, `process`. `game` is `FFX`, `FFX-2`, `both`, `n/a` (decided from the sources, AGENTS.md rule 14). `decisions` links the D- (and early E-) ids the row carries out. `result` says whether it is done, shipped in which release, on a branch, parked, reverted or failed and why.
4. The repository is public: no email addresses (write "account #1", "#2" or "#3"), no card or payment details, no account ids, tokens or keys, no other personal projects, nothing else private to the owner. The validator refuses an email address, a 32-character hex id and card-like digits.

The log runs from round 2 checkpoint (2026-09-17) to both games (2026-10-09).
- **Reviews:** 127 rows: 37 focused reviews (36 SHIP, 1 HOLD), 44 live checks (42 PASS, 1 FAIL, 1 UNVERIFIED), 19 deep rounds with a report (10 SHIP, 6 HOLD, 3 no verdict) and 27 other reviews (critic rounds 02, 03 and 14, paper preflights, visual passes, real-game checks, the round 21 capture hand-off and independent fidelity checks of a build).
- **Not finished or not shipped:** 43 rows end as built on a branch and not merged, parked, pending, in progress or failed; the result line says which.

  - What: Carries out D-566, D-571 and D-578 (no downloads were made). The lane (Sonnet; PCSX2 v2.8.2, the NTSC-U disc, its own save in the card copy) found how the engine starts a scripted battle and forced them: the formation table is at \[0x314218\] (14-byte entries, the scene name in bytes 6 to 13); in any loaded field state, write the formation index to s16 0x315A9E, zero 0x315AA0 and 0x315AA1, and write u8 0x314132 = 2, and the battle starts with the real positions (a forced Omnis matched the walked state to 0.4 units; Evrae's positions matched the static table exactly). Natus was reached by walking. The table is dumped (formation\_table.json) with the script force\_battle.py. Settled: Anima's engine height E (+0x58C) is 138.0 with the script scale at 0.7, so E is NOT multiplied by the script scale (the head joint, 96.26, is 0.70 times 137.5); Omnis's static 178.6 is right (silhouette 172 to 180, best 176), re-derived from the earlier lane's shots with a pose-independent ruler, so a recomputation and not a fresh measurement. Heights in game units above the party floor, ratio to Tidus 18.0: Seymour at Macalania 20.5 (1.14), Guado Guardians 20.5, Anima 96.3 (5.35), Evrae 193 largest extent (10.7, low to medium), Natus 46.2 (2.57), Flux 113 (6.3), Yunalesca form 1 about 20, Braska's Final Aeon 96.2 (5.35; the static 204.7 is more than twice too big), the pagodas about 85, Sin core 27.0, Genais 77.6, the fins and face kept at the static law (low), Omnis 176 (9.8), the Mortiphasm discs 117 across. The independent check recomputed the numbers from the save states and confirmed the two settled checks and the housekeeping, but several cells are overstated: Anima's "silhouette 85" is a clipped region, Yunalesca form 1 rests on wrong rows (about 24 with the wings, 16.4 for the woman), Sin core and Genais rest on joints and an idle maximum, Evrae's 193 and Yunalesca's final 150 are extents and not heights, and the Mortiphasm and pagoda figures are averages.   - What: Carries out D-564, D-574 and D-578 (from 17:21 to about 18:20 EDT; a sub-agent, Sonnet, under the driver; its report was saved by the driver because the harness refuses a sub-agent's report file). Facts only; nothing from the games is in the repo. The size multiplier lives in each model's PS2-era .chr file (a params block; the scale C), not in the monster record, the formation, the HD model or the object's scale vector, and the law is: a model's world size is the raw HD mesh size times C times the AI script's scale vector (default 1). That answers the Yojimbo puzzle: raw 6.775 times C 4.0 is 27.1, the live head point reads 26.9 to 27.0, and 29.0 is a design height. C is 1 for 262 FFX models, 4 for 124 (the aeons and most bosses) and a few larger; in FFX-2 1 for 378, 4 for 46, 2 for about 20 (Vegnagun's parts, the dragons), and every girl is 1. Real heights (game units; Tidus 18.15, the FFX-2 girls' default mean 17.02): FFX-2 Ormi 19.6, Logos 21.4, Leblanc 17.8, Dr. Goon 18.7, Fem-Goon 17.1, Trema 17.8, Shiva 34.4, the Magus Sisters 14.7, 22.9 and 12.5, Ixion 31.6, the Paragon and Oversoul 94.3, Bahamut 87.8, Anima 136.6, Vegnagun about 173 for the whole machine; FFX Yojimbo 27.1, Daigoro 8.0, Lady Ginnem 17.3, Seymour 22.9, Natus 42.0, Flux 100.5, Braska's Final Aeon 204.7, Evrae 208.6, Omnis 178.6, Sin's face 1,701. The finding behind it: the colour chain never applied the sRGB encode, so every painting was drawn with its gamma applied twice; with the encode the figures reproduce their paintings to a mean CIEDE2000 of 2.5 to 3.7, against 12.9 to 15.9 before. Costs he accepted: figures read paler and calmer, Bahamut's wings go from deep red to the painting's salmon; his dark body also lifts toward charcoal and that part stays open. - **A-0452** · `implementation` · both · **Lane r391-stalls: masters upload to the graphics card ahead of their frame in bands, so no master swap lands mid-turn (both games)**
  - What: Release 39 swapped a 2x, 3x or 4x master into a painting's texture in place and Three uploaded it inside the next render: 145 ms for a 4096-square figure master and 193 to 216 ms for a 5376 x 3072 backdrop, on the frame that drew it; a pose never drawn before paid the same at its first draw. The lane (branch r391-stalls from release 39; paper preflight docs/plans/r391-stalls-review.md first, because the change is deep-class) decodes the master off the main thread, uploads it ahead in row bands of 1.3 to 1.7 ms and lets the painting adopt the finished GL texture between two draws (Three's Source sharing). A warm pool uploads paintings before their first draw (capped at the smaller of 640 MB and 30 percent of the class's texture budget), a slow call over 6 ms cuts the next 8 frames' budget to a quarter, ?stage=off is the kill switch and WebKit keeps the old path. Measured on the production code in headless GPU Chromium, the first three real-key turns at 1440p of Chapters I, IV and VIII: GL texture calls over 5 ms 18, 11 and 12 down to 1, 0 and 0; frames over 50 ms that carry an upload 13, 9 and 8 down to 4, 0 and 0. Level 0 of every governed texture is byte-identical to the legacy upload; on screen 0 to 311 of 3.69 million pixels differ, by at most 1 of 255. Costs: Chapter I's first menu holds 1,338 MB of textures against 715 MB, and the first sharp master lands from 1.4 s earlier to 1.0 s later. The frames still over 50 ms are CPU tasks in the game's own tick, not uploads. Both games: shared plumbing, nothing reads a game id.
  - Who: lane sub-agent (Sonnet) under the driver session · Decisions: D-385, D-440
  - Result: done on branch r391-stalls (94e01a00), merged at e37c2df4 and live in release 39.1; the deep review saw the fix hold in Chapters I, Anima and Trema but not lower the FFX-2 slow frames in Vegnagun and Fallen Aeons

Root cause by running the engine: GradeShader is the composer's last pass, a raw ShaderMaterial with no colour-space fragment, and the composer's targets are linear, so the sRGB encode is never applied and every painting's gamma is applied twice; with every pass neutral and the encode added, 11 of 11 figures reproduce their painting to median dE00 0.8 to 2.4 (8.5 to 23 without). F plus, CAS and the hi-res tiers are not causes. In the repo: a default-OFF switch (?figtrue=0..1 or \_\_pyrefly.fx.figureTrue), 0 of 3,686,400 pixels differing with it off; on, figures show their painting's colour, take no bloom and have their rim cut, which is paler and calmer than today (Bahamut's wings go from deep red to dusty salmon). Merged switched off (3cb9c520); a later fix for the switch-on bloom (ef0868b5) is not in release 39.
